# Kindling α00b: Foundations and checks

## What is new

- The numbers every part of the game will build on: maths, game time with the 60-day year, and chance. They give exactly the same bits on your phone, in the browser and on the build computer, so a world will play out the same everywhere and any problem can be replayed.
- The test card has a new square, right of the checker: green means your phone's maths and random draws match the build computer's bit for bit.
- Behind the scenes, the checks that now guard every change before it joins the main version: which parts of the code may use which, banned shortcuts, the project documents and their links, and the review before each merge.

## What to try

1. Tap **Download and install** at the top of this page. It installs over α00, so no uninstall this time. Open Kindling.
2. Look right of the checker: the square should be green.
3. If the square is red, a box with a code appears: tap Copy and paste the code into your reply.
4. Everything else is as before: the checker even, the grey steps, the orange bar sliding, and turning the phone keeps the pixel size.
5. Open the web link: the same green square in the browser.

## What is rough

- There is still no world, only the test card. Colour from light, the game's pixel font and the top strip come next (α01a); the ground follows (α01b).
- The green square checks 16 maths functions at 1,000 values each, 10,000 random draws and a few long sums, about a millisecond at start.

## IDs delivered

`TIM-16` (part: chance keyed to world, system, purpose, subject and moment), `TIM-14` (part: dates), `TIM-18` (part: the rule for game lengths), `RES-05` (part: maths and draws equal on the phone, the browser and the cloud), `PRN-14` (part: layering checked), `PRC-07` (part: the commit check), `PRC-09` (part: the merge gate and the review checklist), `PRC-10` (part: the checks before work joins), `PRC-12` (part: the coverage check and its self-test).
